related_questions.question: When perfect capital markets the total value of a firm should not depend on its capital structure?
related_questions.snippet: Modigliani and Miller (1958) argued that in perfect capital markets the total value of the firm should not depend on its capital structure. The firm's cash flows equal exactly the cash flows generated by the firm's debt and (levered) equity. Therefore they should have the same value (law of one price).
